deviations: Academic performance index uses the dataset's provided PCAperf variable (first principal component of GPA, exams passed, eligible to continue) rather than recomputing the PCA.
GPA uses the dataset's provided standardized GPA variable as is.
notes: Data: uctdata_balanced.dta (499 students x 2 rounds); working sample = round 2 rows (499: 332 black, 117 white, 18 coloured, 32 Indian/other). Treatment mixracebas; cluster on roomnum_base (unique room id). Own controls: Female, Falseuct2012, durpcabas_nomiss, consbas_nomiss, Foreign, privateschool_nomiss plus their missing dummies (foreign_missing and privateschool_miss are all zero and drop out). Roommate controls: the ro* versions of the same (no female) plus missing dummies. Table 3: follow-up DscoreraceIAT on mixracebas + DscoreraceIATbas + controls | residence FE, by race. Table 4: outcome (GPA, examspassed, continue, PCAperf) on mixracebas + controls | residence FE + regprogram FE (panels A/B); panel C adds white/coloured/Else dummies and race-group (black/white/other) x residence FE + program FE. Estimated with fixest feols, clustered by room. Attempts 1-2 were exploratory (variable listing, coding checks; no RESULT lines). Attempt-3 printed RESULT lines using fixest's default singleton removal, which dropped observations alone in a program FE cell (No. Obs. 493 for panel C); I revised to fixef.rm='none' so the estimation sample matches OLS with dummies (No. Obs. 499). This was a methodological self-review, not a comparison with claimed values; coefficients are identical between attempt-3 and the final run, only the panel C count and SEs changed. Note: while reading the paper's method sections (sections 2-5) for specification details, the narrative text displayed some reported point estimates (e.g. the Table 3 white coefficient and Table 4 black GPA coefficient are quoted in section 5 prose); I did not search for them and did not tune anything toward them. Exploration and runs were quick; no hang.
